What are some major differences between GTA5 on PS3 and on PS4?

I noticed pop-in was an issue on the PS3, but that may be more attributed to the speed of the hdd installed in the PS3. If you install a hybrid drive or ssd, pop-in might be reduced. Check YouTube for some videos of the completely retarded effects pop-in can have (crashing into invisible objects that appear only after the crash, etc).

Edit: This video is an excellent example.

I haven't noticed much for issues on the PS4, mind you I have hybrid drives in both my PS3 and PS4, so your experience might differ. I think an ssd is the only thing that can really combat load times though.

HDD speed doesn't make much of a difference on gaming other than start up and load times. The main issue with pop-in, which is a draw distance issue, on the PS3 (and slightly on the PS4, console draw distance isn't great, but GTA V isn't a great game for draw distance, even on a powerful PC because of texture pop-ins and just, yeah) Basically, the PS4 is more powerful the PS3, and as such draw distance is improved, so you already see the buildings from further away and they don't just appear in front of you thanks to the better hardware.

The speed of the hdd has everything to do with latency in loading anything in the game. The PS3 only has 256MB of RAM dedicated to the game, so it must stream-load textures constantly from the hdd as you pass from one area to the next. If your hdd can't keep up, you'll get a reduced framerate and texture pop-ins. The PS4 has 8GB of RAM, up to 5.5GB can be dedicated to the game. That allows for a huge buffer for loading, unlike the PS3.

I had an ssd in my PS3 for a while and was surprised at how snappy everything was, including the PS Store (which had a notoriously bad frame rate and loading), however the ssd cost more than the PS3 so I switched it to a hybrid drive.

Ah. OK. I did not know that the PS3 had such a dismal amount of RAM dedicated to the game. So yes, in this instance you're right, the HDD speed will make a difference, but for current-gen consoles and PC, HDD speed will only affect load times, once everything's loaded, it shouldn't make a difference really.
